newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine air force cuts airports' safety ratings.
newsitem.headline: Argentine air force cuts airports' safety ratings.

text.p: Argentina's air force has recommended that airlines stop flying jets to 18 provincial airports around the country due to insufficient fire-fighting equipment, an air force spokesman said Wednesday.
Airlines are free not to accept the recommendation, the spokesman told Reuters, although the air force is responsable for control of Argentina's civil aviation.

The air force also recommended that larger jets should not fly to the airports of Neuquen, Corrientes and Rosario. Rosario is now used as an alternative landing site for international flights to Buenos Aires in case of bad weather.

Representives of Argentina's three biggest airlines -- Aerolineas Argentinas, Austral and LAPA, which between them carry out 80 percent of domestic flights, told the La Nacion newspaper they planned no changes to their schedules.
"Protection against fire is very important but not vital for operations," said LAPA president Gustavo Deutsch.

The air force's announcement came after a series of public complaints by airline pilots of insufficient fire safety measures and air traffic control, and a spate of near mid-air collisions in Argentina. The government hopes to privatize the country's airports this year.
